about: Facts for the public 'Become a substitute' page. Every entry names its source and the date it was last checked (verified_on). Re-check entries older than 120 days; the settings screen lists them.

steps: Check whether you need fingerprints: only if you lived, worked or studied outside Wisconsin (another state, a US territory, Canada or Great Britain) in the last 20 years since age 17. If so, book Fieldprint (fieldprintwisconsin.com, code FPWIDPITeach) and pay about $40.

Scan your documents as PDF, Word, JPG or text, 2 MB or smaller each: an official transcript and your substitute-training certificate (or form PI-1633 if a district trained you; form PI-1975 if you're on the educator-program path).

Sign in to ELO (Educator Licensing Online), answer the setup questions, then choose 1-Teacher Category → S-Teacher – Short Term Substitute License [T910] → Request Short-term Substitute License [1910], attach your documents and submit.

Wait for DPI's confirmation email, then choose “Submit C&C and Payment”: answer the 14 Conduct & Competency questions and pay $135 by Mastercard, Visa or Discover credit card (no debit cards, no refunds).

Track the application on DPI's status page. Typical processing is 6–8 weeks, 8–12 if you've lived out of state. Meanwhile, keep going with employer applications: they don't wait on the permit, only your first day of work does.
tips: ELO is offline every Wednesday 10 pm to Thursday 2 am.
DPI runs its own background check on every application; an employer's check doesn't replace it.
Your permit lasts 3 years. Renew it in ELO with a new application before it expires.
dpi.employer_onboarding_note: Estimate: EDUStaff applicants report about 2 weeks from application to activation.

permit_a.name: Three-Year Short-Term Substitute Teacher Permit — degree path
permit_a.who: Associate degree or higher, plus a DPI-approved substitute teacher training course (a bachelor's degree doesn't exempt you from the training).
permit_a.allows: Any subject and grade, up to 45 consecutive days in one assignment. Valid 3 years.

permit_b.name: Three-Year Short-Term Substitute Teacher Permit — educator-program path
permit_b.who: Age 20 or older, enrolled in a Wisconsin approved educator preparation program (junior standing if it leads to a bachelor's), with 15 hours of classroom observation. Your program confirms this on form PI-1975. No separate training course is required.
permit_b.allows: Any subject and grade, up to 45 consecutive days in one assignment. Valid 3 years.

long_term.name: Five-Year Long-Term Substitute License
long_term.who: Completed an approved educator preparation program and hold, or are eligible for, a Wisconsin (or equivalent) teaching license. Retired teachers whose license expired can use this route.
long_term.allows: Long-term assignments in your license area, plus short-term (45 days or less) outside it. Valid 5 years.

none.name: Not eligible for a substitute teacher permit yet
none.who: DPI's permits need at least an associate degree, or enrollment in an educator preparation program.
none.allows: Options: finish an associate degree (Wisconsin technical colleges offer Foundations of Teacher Education), or start as a paraprofessional or support-staff substitute, which many districts and EDUStaff also hire for.

long_term_note: A permit caps you at 45 consecutive days in one assignment. Longer assignments need the Five-Year Long-Term Substitute License in that subject, or a One-Year License with Stipulations that the district requests ($140, and you must enroll in an educator program). Special-education assignments over 45 days need a special-education license.

training.next: Scheduled after you apply to EDUStaff
Start any time; pass the assessment with 85%

training.tied: The district confirms it on form PI-1633
